notes: Cross-verse split with JOB.37.22. Both verses write a nominal that the ASV realizes a second time as a resumptive subject pronoun in a following clause of the same verse: אֱלוֹהַּ → *God ... him* at 37.22, שַׁדַּי → *the Almighty ... He* here. 37.22 gives both realizations to the one noun under rule 25; this verse instead folded the resuming *He* into the predicate adjective's unit. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, and rule 25 rules directly: such a pronoun is not added and does not join the predicate's unit, because rule 20 hands the predicate only the construction's copula and, in a presentative clause, its dummy *there*, and a referential pronoun is neither — it goes to the morpheme that denotes it. The *He* is moved into שַׁדַּי's discontinuous unit, headed on the first English occurrence; שַׂגִּיא keeps *is excellent*.
